assignedReviews.card_evidence: A type of white blood cell called a phagocyte surrounds a germ and swallows it whole
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a white blood cell, which is part of blood, but it does not identify the parts of the circulatory system (heart, blood vessels) or describe how the circulatory system works. The focus is on immune defense, not circulatory system structure/function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A type of white blood cell called a phagocyte surrounds a germ and swallows it whole
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a cellular activity (phagocytosis) but does not use a labeled diagram or describe connections between levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere. It only touches on a cell-level process without addressing the organizational hierarchy.

copy.en:
How does the body fight off germs?

A type of white blood cell called a phagocyte surrounds a germ and swallows it whole, eating it up until it's destroyed.
copy.tl:
Paano nilalaban ng katawan ang mga germs?

May uri ng white blood cell na tinatawag na phagocyte na binabalot at nilalamon ang germ, kinakain ito hanggang masira.
copy.bis:
Unsaon sa lawas pagpakig-away sa mga germ?

Adunay matang sa white blood cell nga gitawag og phagocyte nga molibot ug molamoy sa germ, ginakaon kini hangtod malaglag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's tested on many volunteers over a long time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize the features of a fair test and that scientific investigations also involve doing at least three trials, or use replication, and observing, measuring, and recording accurately
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions testing on many volunteers, which loosely relates to replication, but it does not teach the features of a fair test, the need for at least three trials, or accurate observing, measuring, and recording. It is about vaccine safety testing, not the scientific investigation methodology described in the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's tested on many volunteers over a long time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the steps of a simple science investigation (What is the problem? What materials do you need? What do you need to do? What have you found out/learned?)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes vaccine testing but does not outline the steps of a simple science investigation (problem, materials, procedure, findings). It provides no instructional support for the competency's specific steps.

copy.en: Before a vaccine reaches you, it's tested on many volunteers over a long time, with scientists and doctors watching closely to make sure it's safe and it works.
copy.tl: Bago maabot sa iyo ang isang bakuna, sinusubukan muna ito sa maraming boluntaryo sa mahabang panahon, habang mahigpit na binabantayan ng mga siyentista at doktor kung ligtas at gumagana ito.
copy.bis: Sa dili pa moabot kanimo ang usa ka bakuna, sulayan una kini sa daghang boluntaryo sulod sa taas nga panahon, samtang hugot nga bantayan sa mga siyentista ug doktor kon luwas ug molihok ba kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scientists discovered a whole hidden world of tiny living things, like bacteria and yeast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria and yeast as tiny living things discovered with better microscopes, but it does not teach the unicellular vs multicellular distinction or state that bacteria are single-celled. It shares vocabulary and context but gives no direct instructional support for recognizing single-celled vs many-celled organisms.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When microscope lenses got better in the 1600s
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the uses of various science equipment and materials used in simple activities, such as a ruler, hand lens, scissors, balloons, modeling clay, and cardboard
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to microscope lenses improving, but it does not describe the uses of science equipment or materials in simple activities, nor does it mention a ruler, hand lens, scissors, or similar items. The microscope is only historical context, not instruction on equipment use.

copy.en: When microscope lenses got better in the 1600s, scientists discovered a whole hidden world of tiny living things, like bacteria and yeast.
copy.tl: Nang gumanda ang mga lente ng mikroskopyo noong 1600s, natuklasan ng mga siyentipiko ang bagong mundo ng maliliit na nilalang tulad ng bakterya at lebadura.
copy.bis: Sa dihang niayo ang mga lente sa mikroskopyo niadtong 1600s, nadiskobrehan sa mga siyentista ang bag-ong kalibutan sa gagmayng buhi sama sa bakterya ug lebadura.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Incomplete dominance isn't only in snapdragons — carnation colors can blend together, and radish offspring can grow a shape in between long and round.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes incomplete dominance (blending of traits), not a simple dominant/recessive characteristic, and does not represent inheritance through generations of a family.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Incomplete dominance isn't only in snapdragons — carnation colors can blend together, and radish offspring can grow a shape in between long and round.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict simple ratios of offspring genotypes and phenotypes in crosses involving dominant/recessive gene pairs
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives examples of blended phenotypes but provides no genotypes, crosses, or ratios involving dominant/recessive gene pairs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Incomplete dominance isn't only in snapdragons — carnation colors can blend together, and radish offspring can grow a shape in between long and round.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates a trait transmission pattern but does not explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in transmitting traits.

copy.en: Incomplete dominance isn't only in snapdragons — carnation colors can blend together, and radish offspring can grow a shape in between long and round.
copy.tl: Hindi lang sa snapdragon makikita ang incomplete dominance — sa carnation, naghahalo ang kulay, at sa labanos, lumalabas sa supling ang anyong nasa gitna ng mahaba at bilog.
copy.bis: Dili lang sa snapdragon makita ang incomplete dominance — sa carnation, magsagol ang kolor, ug sa labanos, motungha sa anak ang porma nga taliwala sa taas ug lingin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The index of refraction for water is about 1.33, and for glass, it's about 1.5.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a refractive index fact and compares light speed in water and glass, which is related to refraction. However, the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection/refraction using mirrors, transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with everyday applications. The card does not describe an investigation, use any of the specified equipment, or illustrate the phenomena, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How does light speed compare in water and glass?

The index of refraction for water is about 1.33, and for glass, it's about 1.5. This means light travels more slowly in glass than in water!
copy.tl:
Paano nagkumpara ang bilis ng liwanag sa tubig at salamin?

Ang index of refraction ng tubig ay halos 1.33, at ng salamin ay halos 1.5. Ibig sabihin, mas mabagal ang liwanag sa salamin kaysa sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsa magkompara ang tulin sa suga sa tubig ug salamin?

Ang index of refraction sa tubig mga 1.33, ug sa salamin mga 1.5. Nagpasabot kini nga mas hinay ang suga sa salamin kaysa sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It zoomed into the Martian sky and made its historic first flight in the year 2021!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Mars helicopter, a space technology, but only states the year of its first flight. It does not explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies such as telescopes and space probes, nor does it discuss the role of Ingenuity in research.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It zoomed into the Martian sky and made its historic first flight in the year 2021!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to Mars, a celestial object in the solar system, but provides no information about the general structure of the solar system, names of major celestial objects, their features, or composition. It only gives a single fact about a Mars mission.

copy.en:
When did the Ingenuity helicopter take its very first flight on Mars?

It zoomed into the Martian sky and made its historic first flight in the year 2021!
copy.tl:
Kailan unang lumipad ang Ingenuity helicopter sa Mars?

Lumipad ito sa kalangitan ng Mars at ginawa ang makasaysayang unang paglipad noong taong 2021!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a unang milupad ang Ingenuity helicopter sa Mars?

Milupad kini sa langit sa Mars ug gihimo ang makasaysayang unang paglupad sa tuig 2021!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Insects use their antennae to smell and feel the world around them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an outer body part (antennae) but describes its role in sensing (smell and touch), not the roles specified in the competency (move and gather food). It does not directly support the competency's action of identifying roles for movement or food gathering.

copy.en: Insects use their antennae to smell and feel the world around them.
copy.tl: Ginagamit ng mga insekto ang kanilang antenyo para maamoy at mahipo ang paligid nila.
copy.bis: Gigamit sa mga insekto ang ilang antenyo aron makaamgo ug makabati sa ilang palibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Insect blood is called hemolymph and is usually yellow or clear, not red
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Insect hemolymph is not muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory as a set.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: because insects don't use hemoglobin; their tracheal system delivers oxygen directly to tissues
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Insect blood color is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en:
Is insect blood red like ours?

Nope! Insect blood is called hemolymph and is usually yellow or clear, not red — because insects don't use hemoglobin; their tracheal system delivers oxygen directly to tissues.
copy.tl:
Pula ba ang dugo ng insekto?

Hindi pala! Ang dugo ng insekto ay tinatawag na hemolymph, karaniwang dilaw o malinaw, hindi pula — dahil hindi gumagamit ng hemoglobin ang insekto; ang tracheal system nito ang nagdadala ng oxygen diretso sa tissue.
copy.bis:
Pula ba ang dugo sa insekto?

Dili diay! Ang dugo sa insekto gitawag og hemolymph, kasagaran dilaw o klaro, dili pula — kay ang insekto wala naggamit og hemoglobin; ang tracheal system niini ang direktang nagdala og oxygen sa tissue.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Insects see through compound eyes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes insect compound eyes and mosaic vision. While eyes are an outer body part, the competency specifically targets head, legs, or wings and their role in movement and food gathering. The card does not address those parts or their roles, so it only shares the broad subject of animal body parts.

copy.en:
How do insects see the world?

Insects see through compound eyes made of hundreds of tiny lenses, creating a wide mosaic view of everything around them.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakakita ang insekto?

Ang mga insekto ay may compound eyes na binubuo ng daan-daang maliliit na lente na nagbibigay ng mosaic na pangitain sa kanilang paligid.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkakita sa insekto?

Ang mga insekto adunay compound eyes nga gilangkoban og gatusan ka gagmay nga lente nga naghatag og mosaic nga panan-aw sa ilang palibot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: silk moth larvae — each cocoon unwinds into a single silk thread
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions larvae and cocoon, which are life-cycle stages, but it does not use a flow chart to compare stages of an animal's life cycle. The focus is on silk thread length, not on comparing developmental stages. Format requirement (flow chart) is not met, and the content does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How long is one silk thread?

The world's silk comes from silk moth larvae — each cocoon unwinds into a single silk thread over 300 meters long!
copy.tl:
Gaano kahaba ang sinulid ng silkworm?

Mula sa larva ng silk moth galing ang sutlang ginagamit sa buong mundo — ang isang cocoon ay may iisang tuloy-tuloy na sinulid na mahigit 300 metro ang haba!
copy.bis:
Unsa kataas ang hilo sa silkworm?

Gikan sa larva sa silk moth ang sutla nga gigamit sa tibuok kalibutan — ang usa ka cocoon adunay usa lang ka tuluy-tuloyon nga hilo nga labaw sa 300 metros ang gitas-on!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An insect's six legs and its wings all attach to one spot — the thorax, the middle part of its body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states where an insect's legs and wings attach (the thorax). It does not describe the outer body parts themselves or identify their role in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of G3-L-4. The content is topically related to animal body parts but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's stated skill.

copy.en: An insect's six legs and its wings all attach to one spot — the thorax, the middle part of its body.
copy.tl: Ang anim na paa at mga pakpak ng insekto ay kabit lahat sa iisang bahagi — ang thorax o gitnang bahagi ng katawan.
copy.bis: Ang unom ka tiil ug mga pako sa insekto tanan nakabit sa usa lang ka bahin — ang thorax o tunga nga bahin sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It only slows heat from moving so the temperature lasts longer!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that insulation slows heat transfer, which is a general heat-transfer concept, but it does not identify examples of conduction, convection, or radiation, nor does it discuss advantageous or disadvantageous examples of these specific modes. It only addresses insulation's effect on temperature retention.

copy.en:
Does insulation actually make things cold?

No! Insulation does not make cold. It only slows heat from moving so the temperature lasts longer!
copy.tl:
Gumagawa ba ng lamig ang insulasyon?

Hindi! Hindi gumagawa ng lamig ang insulasyon. Pinapabagal lang nito ang paglipat ng init para magtagal ang temperatura!
copy.bis:
Mohimo ba ug bugnaw ang insulasyon?

Dili! Ang insulasyon dili maghimo ug bugnaw. Magpahinay lang kini sa paglihok sa kainit aron molungtad ang temperatura!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When there's too little insulin, or it stops working well, blood sugar rises
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a cause of diabetes via insulin and rising blood sugar, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or address the listed indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure) as indicators of homeostasis. It only touches on blood sugar, which is one indicator, without teaching the homeostasis concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When there's too little insulin, or it stops working well, blood sugar rises
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions insulin's role in blood sugar but does not explain feedback mechanisms, positive or negative, or how homeostasis is maintained. It provides no information about regulation loops, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
What causes diabetes to develop?

When there's too little insulin, or it stops working well, blood sugar rises — and that's how a person can develop diabetes.
copy.tl:
Ano ang sanhi ng diabetes?

Kapag kulang ang insulin o hindi ito gumagana nang maayos, tumataas ang asukal sa dugo — at ito ang dahilan kung bakit nagkakaroon ng diabetes.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang hinungdan sa diabetes?

Kung kulang ang insulin o dili kini molihok og maayo, motaas ang asukal sa dugo — ug mao kini ang hinungdan ngano nga mahimong magka-diabetes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When two waves meet, they can add together in constructive interference or cancel out in destructive interference!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out investigations with water waves in a ripple tank and observe and describe the features of the waves including shape (crests and troughs), size (width and height), and patterns of movement (how they bend, or reflect off walls)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses wave interference, but G6-F-5 requires carrying out ripple tank investigations and describing wave features like crests/troughs, width/height, and bending/reflection. No such investigation or feature description is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When two waves meet, they can add together in constructive interference or cancel out in destructive interference!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about wave interference, not about waves carrying energy from a source to a receiver. No mention of energy transfer is made.

copy.en: When two waves meet, they can add together in constructive interference or cancel out in destructive interference! Noise-cancelling headphones actually use destructive interference to block sound.
copy.tl: Kapag nagtatagpo ang dalawang alon, pwede silang magdagdag sa constructive interference o mag-cancel sa destructive interference! Gumagamit ang noise-cancelling headphones ng destructive interference para i-block ang tunog.
copy.bis: Kung magkupon ang duha ka alon, mahimo silang magdugang sa constructive interference o mag-cancel sa destructive interference! Ang noise-cancelling headphones naggamit sa destructive interference para i-block ang tunog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In just seconds, we can find, send, and share information, news, pictures, and messages with almost anyone in the world!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies the internet as a science invention and describes its impact (fast sharing of information), which matches the core concept of the competency. However, the competency specifically requires using information from the home or local community to identify the invention and explain its impact. The card provides no guidance or activity involving home or community sources, so it does not directly support the stated skill at this placement.

copy.en:
How did the internet change life?

In just seconds, we can find, send, and share information, news, pictures, and messages with almost anyone in the world!
copy.tl:
Paano binago ng internet ang buhay?

Sa loob ng ilang segundo, makakahanap, makakapagpadala, at makakapagbahagi na tayo ng impormasyon, balita, larawan, at mensahe sa kahit sinong tao sa mundo!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pag-usab sa internet ang kinabuhi?

Sulod sa pipila ka segundo, makakita, makapadala, ug makapakigbahin na kita og impormasyon, balita, hulagway, ug mensahe sa halos bisan kinsa sa kalibutan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Keeping nails short and clean stops worm eggs from collecting and hiding underneath them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card is a hygiene tip about preventing worm eggs under nails. It does not explain interactions between living things or between living and non-living things bringing good or harm in an ecosystem sense; it is health advice rather than instruction on the competency.

copy.en:
How do short nails help stop worms?

Keeping nails short and clean stops worm eggs from collecting and hiding underneath them.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakatulong ang maiksing kuko laban sa bulate?

Ang pagpapaikli at paglilinis ng kuko ay nakakatulong upang hindi makaipon ang itlog ng bulate sa ilalim nito.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtabang sa mubo nga kuko batok sa bulate?

Ang pagpamutol ug paglimpyo sa kuko makatabang aron dili makatigom ang itlog sa bulate sa ilalom niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pinworms crawl out at night to lay their eggs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific parasite laying eggs, but the competency requires identifying which groups of animals reproduce by live birth versus egg-laying (e.g., mammals vs. birds/reptiles). The card does not provide group-level classification or contrast, so it only shares the general concept of egg-laying without directly supporting the competency.

copy.en:
Why do pinworms make you itchy at night?

Pinworms crawl out at night to lay their eggs, which is why it feels itchy then — and why doctors sometimes check for them early in the morning.
copy.tl:
Bakit nangangati sa gabi dahil sa pinworm?

Ang pinworm ay lumalabas tuwing gabi para mangitlog, kaya nangangati doon sa gabi — at kaya rin minsan tinitingnan ito ng doktor kapag madaling-araw.
copy.bis:
Nganong makatol sa gabii tungod sa pinworm?

Ang pinworm mogawas sa gabii aron mangitlog, mao nga makatol didto sa gabii — ug mao usab nga usahay susihon kini sa doktor sa kaadlawon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water hyacinth can double the area it covers in just a few weeks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the rapid growth of water hyacinth, an invasive species, but does not describe the possible effects of human activities on living things in an ecosystem. It lacks any mention of human introduction, pollution, or consequences for other organisms. It only states a growth fact, which is background knowledge about an invasive species rather than direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en:
How fast can water hyacinth grow?

In warm, nutrient-rich water, water hyacinth can double the area it covers in just a few weeks — which is how a small patch takes over a whole lake!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis lumaki ang water hyacinth?

Sa mainit at maruming tubig na maraming sustansya, madoble ng water hyacinth ang sakop nito sa loob lang ng ilang linggo — kaya't kaya nitong takpan ang malaking bahagi ng lawa!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadali motubo ang water hyacinth?

Sa init ug hugaw nga tubig nga daghan og sustansya, madoble sa water hyacinth ang gisakpan niini sulod ra sa pipila ka semana — mao nga matabonan niini ang dakong bahin sa lanaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lack of iodine causes goiter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a nutrient (iodine) and a health condition, but does not teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) or how those needs are met. It is only tangentially related to food/nutrition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a swelling in the neck
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Goiter is a swelling in the neck, but the card does not describe how any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) works. It mentions a symptom but provides no instruction on body system function.

copy.en: Lack of iodine causes goiter, a swelling in the neck — that's why the Philippines uses iodized salt to keep everyone healthy!
copy.tl: Ang kakulangan sa iodine ay nagdudulot ng goiter, isang pamamaga sa leeg — kaya gumagamit ang Pilipinas ng iodized salt para maging malusog ang lahat!
copy.bis: Ang kakulang sa iodine mohatag og goiter, usa ka pamamaga sa liog — mao nga naggamit ang Pilipinas og iodized salt aron himsog ang tanan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pregnant mothers really need iodine, because their growing baby uses it to build a healthy brain and body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a specific nutrient (iodine) needed during pregnancy, not the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter) as required by G3-L-6. It shares the broad theme of needs but does not directly teach the listed basic needs.

copy.en: Pregnant mothers really need iodine, because their growing baby uses it to build a healthy brain and body.
copy.tl: Kailangang-kailangan ng iodine ng mga buntis na nanay dahil ginagamit ito ng sanggol sa loob ng tiyan para lumaki nang malusog ang utak at katawan nito.
copy.bis: Gikinahanglan gyud sa mga mabdos nga inahan ang iodine kay gigamit kini sa bata sa sulod sa tiyan aron motubo og himsog nga utok ug lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It uses iodine to make a hormone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a hormone from the thyroid, which is part of the endocrine system, but it does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together. It only states a single gland's function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a chemical messenger that tells the body's cells how fast to work
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on regulation of cell activity via a hormone, which is loosely related to homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it mention indicators like body temperature, glucose level, or blood pressure.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It uses iodine to make a hormone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cells and a chemical messenger, but it does not use a labelled diagram to describe connections between levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere. It only refers to cells in passing.

copy.en:
What does the thyroid do with iodine?

It uses iodine to make a hormone — a chemical messenger that tells the body's cells how fast to work!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng thyroid sa iodine?

Ginagamit nito ang iodine para gumawa ng hormone, isang chemical messenger na nagsasabi sa mga selula kung gaano kabilis dapat gumana!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buhaton sa thyroid sa iodine?

Gigamit niini ang iodine aron maghimo og hormone, usa ka chemical messenger nga magsulti sa mga selula kung unsa ka paspas molihok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The positive and negative charges are equal in amount, so they balance out perfectly!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of ions as either the loss or gain of electrons to produce ionic bonds, using examples, such as the formation of sodium chloride
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why an ionic compound is neutral because positive and negative charges balance. It does not explain the formation of ions by loss or gain of electrons, nor the production of ionic bonds, nor use an example such as sodium chloride.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why is an ionic compound neutral even though it's made of charged ions?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical names of some common ionic compounds, including sodium chloride (NaCl), magnesium oxide (MgO), potassium chloride (KCl) and magnesium chloride (MgCl2)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ionic compounds generally but does not provide chemical formulas or names of common ionic compounds such as NaCl, MgO, KCl, or MgCl2.

copy.en:
Why is an ionic compound neutral even though it's made of charged ions?

The positive and negative charges are equal in amount, so they balance out perfectly!
copy.tl:
Bakit neutral ang ionic compound kahit gawa sa mga ion?

Pantay ang dami ng positibo at negatibong singil, kaya nagbabalanse sila nang sempurna!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga neutral ang ionic compound bisan gihimo sa mga ion?

Managsama ang gidaghanon sa positibo ug negatibo nga singil, busa nagbalanse sila nga hingpit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its roots can capture nitrogen straight from the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes roots capturing nitrogen from the air, not roots getting water and nutrients from the soil. It does not address the outer parts of plants (leaves, stems, roots) in the role of obtaining water/nutrients from soil, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its roots can capture nitrogen straight from the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a root function (nitrogen capture) but does not describe the root and shoot system as a whole or explain why they are important in the general sense. It focuses on a specific nitrogen-fixing ability, which is not the core of observing and describing the importance of root and shoot systems.

copy.en:
Why does ipil-ipil enrich the soil?

The ipil-ipil tree enriches soil because its roots can capture nitrogen straight from the air.
copy.tl:
Bakit napapataba ng ipil-ipil ang lupa?

Napapataba ng ipil-ipil ang lupa dahil kaya ng mga ugat nito na kumuha ng nitroheno mula sa hangin.
copy.bis:
Nganong napatambok sa ipil-ipil ang yuta?

Ang ipil-ipil makapatambok sa yuta tungod kay makakuha ang mga gamot niini og nitrogen gikan sa hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a plant lacks iron, young leaves turn yellow between the veins while the veins stay green
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a nutrient deficiency symptom in leaves, not the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) and their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It shares the plant/leaf topic but does not directly support the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a plant lacks iron, young leaves turn yellow between the veins while the veins stay green
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves (part of the shoot system) but does not describe the root and shoot system or why they are important. It is about iron deficiency chlorosis, not the structure and importance of plant systems.

copy.en:
Why do leaf veins stay green but not the rest?

When a plant lacks iron, young leaves turn yellow between the veins while the veins stay green — because iron cannot move from old leaves to new ones.
copy.tl:
Bakit nananatiling berde ang ugat ng dahon?

Kapag kulang sa iron ang halaman, nagiging dilaw ang bahagi sa pagitan ng ugat ng batang dahon, pero nananatiling berde ang mismong mga ugat — dahil hindi kayang ilipat ng halaman ang iron mula sa lumang dahon papunta sa bago.
copy.bis:
Nganong berde gihapon ang ugat sa dahon?

Kon kulang sa iron ang tanom, mahimong dalag ang bahin tunga sa ugat sa batan-on nga dahon, apan magpabilin nga berde ang mga ugat mismo — kay dili makabalhin ang tanom sa iron gikan sa daan nga dahon padulong sa bag-o.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because they grow fast and make lots of new blood!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions making new blood, which touches on the circulatory system, but it does not describe how the circulatory system (or any listed body system) works. It is a nutrition fact about iron, not an explanation of system function.

copy.en:
Why do babies need iron?

Because they grow fast and make lots of new blood! Iron also helps a baby's brain develop well, which is why iron-rich foods matter as kids grow.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng sanggol ang iron?

Dahil mabilis silang lumalaki at gumagawa ng maraming bagong dugo! Tumutulong din ang iron sa paglaki ng utak, kaya mahalaga ang pagkaing mayaman sa iron habang lumalaki ang bata.
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan sa masuso ang iron?

Tungod kay paspas sila motubo ug maghimo og daghang bag-ong dugo! Motabang usab ang iron sa pagtubo sa utok, mao nga importante ang pagkaon nga adunahan sa iron samtang nagdako ang bata.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Iron sinks in water because its density is about 7.9 g/cm³
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions density, which is a physical property, but the competency focuses on describing physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. Density and the sinking behavior are not the targeted properties and do not directly teach this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Iron sinks in water because its density is about 7.9 g/cm³
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density and sinking, not the definition of matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Iron sinks in water because its density is about 7.9 g/cm³, which is much higher than water's!
copy.tl: Lumulubog ang bakal sa tubig dahil mas mataas ang densidad nito (mga 7.9 g/cm³) kaysa sa tubig!
copy.bis: Molugdang ang puthaw sa tubig kay mas taas ang densidad niini (mga 7.9 g/cm³) kaysa sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: develop new rice varieties that resist disease and give bigger harvests
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify examples of modern biotechnology, such as genetically modified organisms and processes (e.g. in vitro fertilization)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions developing new rice varieties but does not specify that this is done through modern biotechnology (e.g., genetic modification). It could be traditional breeding, so it does not directly support identifying examples of modern biotechnology.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: develop new rice varieties that resist disease and give bigger harvests
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the term biotechnology and provide examples
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not explain the term biotechnology or provide an explicit example of biotechnology. It only describes agricultural research, which is related to the broader topic but does not teach the competency.

copy.en: Scientists at IRRI in Los Baños, Laguna, and PhilRice work hard to develop new rice varieties that resist disease and give bigger harvests.
copy.tl: Nagtatrabaho ang mga siyentipiko sa IRRI sa Los Baños, Laguna at sa PhilRice para makagawa ng bagong uri ng palay na matibay sa sakit at may mas maraming ani.
copy.bis: Naghago ang mga siyentista sa IRRI sa Los Baños, Laguna ug sa PhilRice aron makahimo og bag-ong klase sa humay nga makasugakod sa sakit ug adunay mas daghang ani.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it orbits so fast, astronauts on the ISS see about 16 sunrises and sunsets each day!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that the ISS orbits fast, causing multiple sunrises/sunsets. It does not demonstrate Earth's rotation on its axis using a globe, nor does it explain day and night from Earth's rotation. The connection to day/night is only via the occurrence of sunrises, which is a related concept but not the required demonstration or explanation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it orbits so fast, astronauts on the ISS see about 16 sunrises and sunsets each day!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the ISS and its orbit, not about the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, their features, or composition. It does not support the competency at all.

copy.en:
How many sunrises do astronauts see on the ISS each day?

Because it orbits so fast, astronauts on the ISS see about 16 sunrises and sunsets each day!
copy.tl:
Ilang pagsikat ng araw ang nakikita ng mga astronaut sa ISS kada araw?

Dahil napakabilis nitong umiikot, nakikita ng mga astronaut sa ISS ang humigit-kumulang 16 na pagsikat at paglubog ng araw kada araw!
copy.bis:
Pila ka pagsubang sa adlaw ang makita sa mga astronaut sa ISS matag adlaw?

Tungod kay paspas kaayo kini motuyok, ang mga astronaut sa ISS makakita og mga 16 ka pagsubang ug pagsalop sa adlaw matag adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside the ISS, astronauts appear to float because almost everything is weightless in orbit!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses weightlessness in orbit, not gravity as a non-contact force affecting objects on Earth. It does not identify gravity as a force or describe its predictable effects on Earth, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Inside the ISS, astronauts appear to float because almost everything is weightless in orbit!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the appearance of floating due to weightlessness, but does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. It does not address gravity's role in motion, so it is only related to the topic.

copy.en:
Why do astronauts appear to float inside the ISS?

Inside the ISS, astronauts appear to float because almost everything is weightless in orbit!
copy.tl:
Bakit parang lumulutang ang mga astronaut sa loob ng ISS?

Sa loob ng ISS, parang lumulutang ang mga astronaut dahil halos walang bigat ang lahat sa orbit.
copy.bis:
Nganong morag naglutaw ang mga astronaut sulod sa ISS?

Sulod sa ISS, ang mga astronaut morag naglutaw tungod kay halos walay gibug-aton ang tanan sa orbit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ISS orbits the Earth at an altitude of about 400 kilometers above the surface!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the ISS orbital altitude. It does not explain how modern research about celestial objects uses space technologies such as telescopes and space probes. The ISS is a space station, not a telescope or probe, and the card provides no instructional support for the competency's skill.

copy.en:
How high up does the ISS orbit the Earth?

The ISS orbits the Earth at an altitude of about 400 kilometers above the surface!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalayong umiikot ang ISS sa ibabaw ng Mundo?

Umiikot ang ISS sa Mundo sa taas na halos 400 kilometro mula sa ibabaw nito!
copy.bis:
Unsa kataas ang pagtuyok sa ISS ibabaw sa Kalibutan?

Nagtuyok ang ISS sa Kalibutan sa gitas-on nga mga 400 ka kilometro gikan sa ibabaw niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ISS looks like a bright, fast-moving dot in the sky
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on natural celestial objects (Sun, Moon, planets, stars) and their apparent motion. The ISS is an artificial satellite, not one of these objects, so the card does not directly support the skill of exploring and recording the movement of those natural objects.

copy.en: On a clear night, look up! The ISS looks like a bright, fast-moving dot in the sky, even right here in the Philippines!
copy.tl: Sa malinaw na gabi, tumingin sa langit! Ang ISS ay mukhang isang maliwanag at mabilis na tuldok, kahit dito sa Pilipinas!
copy.bis: Sa tin-aw nga gabii, tan-awa ang langit! Ang ISS murag usa ka hayag ug paspas nga tuldok, bisan dinhi sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Raising ducks is a livelihood for many farmers, thanks to the sale of eggs, balut, and salted eggs.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ducks and eggs, but it does not teach that birds reproduce by laying eggs or contrast live birth vs egg-laying. It is about livelihood and egg products, not reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Raising ducks is a livelihood for many farmers, thanks to the sale of eggs, balut, and salted eggs.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ducks but does not provide a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat. It is about duck farming as a livelihood, not habitat classification.

copy.en: Raising ducks is a livelihood for many farmers, thanks to the sale of eggs, balut, and salted eggs.
copy.tl: Ang pag-aalaga ng itik ay hanapbuhay ng maraming magsasaka dahil sa benta ng itlog, balut, at itlog na maalat.
copy.bis: Ang pagbuhi og itik usa ka panginabuhi sa daghang mag-uuma tungod sa baligya sa itlog, balut, ug itlog nga parat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's full of vitamins that help keep kids' bodies healthy and strong!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the nutritional value of jackfruit for children's health. It does not teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) or help students identify those needs. The mention of food is only incidental and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Jackfruit isn't just tasty — it's full of vitamins that help keep kids' bodies healthy and strong!
copy.tl: Hindi lang masarap ang langka — puno ito ng bitamina na tumutulong para maging malusog at malakas ang katawan ng mga bata!
copy.bis: Dili ra lami ang nangka — puno kini og bitamina nga makatabang aron mahimong himsog ug kusgan ang lawas sa mga bata!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the seeds can be cooked too, tasting good like nuts when boiled or roasted
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cooking (boiling/roasting) which involves temperature, but it does not describe any change in material properties. It only states that jackfruit seeds are edible and taste like nuts when cooked. The competency requires describing changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes (e.g., burning wood/coal), which is not addressed.

copy.en: It's not just the yellow flesh of jackfruit we eat — the seeds can be cooked too, tasting good like nuts when boiled or roasted.
copy.tl: Hindi lang ang dilaw na laman ng langka ang kinakain; pwede ring lutuin ang buto nito — masarap itong parang mani kapag pinakuluan o iniihaw.
copy.bis: Dili lang ang dalag nga unod sa nangka ang kan-on; mahimo usab lung-agon o sugbahon ang liso — lami kini sama sa mani.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A jackfruit's skin is green and covered all over with tiny, pointy bumps!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the texture and color of a jackfruit's skin, which is a fruit covering, not one of the outer plant parts named in the competency (leaves, roots, stems). It also does not address the role of these parts in obtaining water and nutrients from the soil. The content is only broadly related to plant parts.

copy.en: A jackfruit's skin is green and covered all over with tiny, pointy bumps!
copy.tl: Ang balat ng langka ay berde at puno ng maliliit at matutulis na bukol!
copy.bis: Ang panit sa nangka berde ug puno sa gagmay ug talinis nga mga bukol!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many think jackfruit and durian are the same
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only compares two fruits and does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, animal groups, microorganisms). It shares the plant topic but provides no direct instructional support for the classification competency.

copy.en:
Are jackfruit and durian the same?

Many think jackfruit and durian are the same because both are big and spiky — but they're different: jackfruit is sweeter and not as smelly as durian!
copy.tl:
Magkapareho ba ang langka at durian?

Maraming akala na iisa lang ang langka at durian dahil parehong malaki at matinik — pero magkaiba sila: mas matamis ang langka at hindi kasing-bahong durian!
copy.bis:
Managsama ba ang nangka ug durian?

Daghan ang naghunahuna nga managsama ra ang nangka ug durian kay parehong dagko ug tunokon — apan lahi sila: mas tam-is ang nangka ug dili kaayo baho sama sa durian!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A ripe jackfruit has such a strong, sweet smell
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a smell of a ripe jackfruit, which is a physical property, but the competency focuses on describing physical properties of solid materials with examples like hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not teach the concept of physical properties or provide the kind of descriptive comparison the competency expects; it merely states a single sensory observation about a fruit.

copy.en: A ripe jackfruit has such a strong, sweet smell that you can notice it from far away!
copy.tl: Ang hinog na langka ay may napakalakas at matamis na amoy na kahit malayo ay mahahalata mo agad!
copy.bis: Ang hinog nga nangka adunay kusog kaayo ug tam-is nga humot nga masimhotan bisan sa layo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the swollen, sick liver can no longer clear a yellow substance out of the blood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Liver jaundice is not muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory as a set.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the swollen, sick liver can no longer clear a yellow substance out of the blood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: A liver pigment in blood is not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en:
Why does skin turn yellow in hepatitis?

The skin turns yellow because the swollen, sick liver can no longer clear a yellow substance out of the blood.
copy.tl:
Bakit nangingilaw ang balat sa hepatitis?

Nangingilaw ang balat dahil hindi na kayang linisin ng namamagang atay ang isang kulay-dilaw na sangkap sa dugo.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga manilaw ang panit sa hepatitis?

Manilaw ang panit kay ang namaga nga atay dili na makawagtang sa dalag nga sangkap sa dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The jeepney is proudly nicknamed the "King of the Road" all across the Philippines!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a nickname for the jeepney. It does not identify the jeepney as a science invention, nor does it explain its impact on everyday life, which are the core actions of G4-M-2.

copy.en: The jeepney is proudly nicknamed the "King of the Road" all across the Philippines!
copy.tl: Ang jeepney ay tinatawag na "King of the Road" o Hari ng Daan sa buong Pilipinas!
copy.bis: Ang jeepney gitawag nga "King of the Road" o Hari sa Dalan sa tibuok Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The box jellyfish lives in the Philippines, and it has a very dangerous sting.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The box jellyfish lives in the Philippines, and it has a very dangerous sting.

assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a Philippine animal but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify it by habitat, and does not address terrestrial/aquatic/aerial classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The box jellyfish lives in the Philippines, and it has a very dangerous sting.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a dangerous sting but does not describe how the animal has changed to suit its environment, such as mimicry or camouflage.

copy.en: The box jellyfish lives in the Philippines, and it has a very dangerous sting.
copy.tl: May uri ng dikya na box jellyfish na matatagpuan sa Pilipinas, at napakapanganib ang kagat nito.
copy.bis: Naa'y matang sa dikya nga box jellyfish nga makit-an sa Pilipinas, ug delikado kaayo ang paak niini.
